description: WatchWater is the citizen alert platform of the Observatoire Tunisien de l'Eau, a project set up in 2016 by the association Nomad 08 to defend the right to water. Residents report unannounced water cuts, network leaks and tap water pollution on a web map, and the observatory publishes a monthly Carte de la soif (thirst map) with counts by type and governorate: for July 2026 it recorded 608 citizen reports, including 549 unannounced cuts and disruptions, 34 protests over water access, 13 leaks and 12 water quality alerts, concentrated in Nabeul, Monastir, Mahdia and Sousse. Coverage is Tunisia. The alert map and the monthly summaries are free on the site in French and Arabic; no bulk download or licence is stated. Caveats: the reports are citizen submissions, and the data are published as a map and blog posts, not a table. Simulation uses: the location and frequency of supply interruptions for resilience analysis and emergency response planning of drinking water service under drought. Related records: the Pacific Institute water conflict chronology (data-pacific-institute-water-conflict-chronology).
